record.original_question: Are the parallel identical machine problems P|r_j, p_j=p|sum w_j U_j and P|r_j, p_j=p|sum U_j fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7. Are P|rj, pj=p|ΣwjUj and P|rj, pj=p|ΣUj fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of machines?

Parallel identical machines (denoted by “P” in the α-field). We are given a number m of parallel identical machines (that is, of the same speed). Each job j has to be processed by exactly one machine for a given amount pj ∈ N of time and each machine can process only one job at a time.
Processing time restrictions. If all jobs j have unit processing time, we add “pj = 1” to the β-field. If all jobs j have an equal processing time p, we add “pj = p” to the β-field.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following parallel-machine scheduling problems.

Setup. We are given m identical parallel machines and n jobs. Every job j has a release date r_j ∈ ℕ, a due date d_j ∈ ℕ, and (in the weighted variant) a weight w_j ∈ ℕ. All jobs share the same processing time p ∈ ℕ. A schedule assigns each job j to exactly one machine and to a starting time s_j ≥ r_j; on each machine, the time intervals [s_j, s_j + p) of the assigned jobs must be pairwise disjoint. A job j is called tardy in a schedule if s_j + p > d_j, in which case U_j = 1, and otherwise U_j = 0.

Two objective functions are considered:
(a) the unweighted number of tardy jobs ∑_{j} U_j,
(b) the weighted number of tardy jobs ∑_{j} w_j U_j.

Denote the corresponding decision/optimization problems in the standard three-field notation by P | r_j, p_j = p | ∑ U_j and P | r_j, p_j = p | ∑ w_j U_j respectively.

Question. Is either of these two problems fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number m of machines? That is, does there exist a computable function f and a constant c such that an optimal schedule can be computed in time f(m) · (n + log(max parameters))^c?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 result (Heeger, Hermelin, Mnich, and Shabtay; published at STACS 2025) proves that P | r_j, p_j = p | ∑ U_j is NP-hard and W[2]-hard when parameterized by the number m of machines, explicitly resolving this open question negatively. As a consequence, the weighted variant P | r_j, p_j = p | ∑ w_j U_j is also W[2]-hard parameterized by m, so neither problem is fixed-parameter tractable in m unless FPT = W[2].

status_evidence.title: Minimizing the Number of Tardy Jobs with Uniform Processing Times on Parallel Machines
status_evidence.snippet: P|r_j,p_j=p|∑U_j is NP-hard and W[2]-hard parameterized by m, resolving Open Problem 7 by Mnich and van Bevern.
status_evidence.claim: The unweighted problem is W[2]-hard parameterized by the number of machines, hence not FPT (unless FPT=W[2]); this also rules out FPT for the weighted variant.

status_evidence.title: Minimizing the Number of Tardy Jobs with Uniform Processing Times on Parallel Machines (STACS 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: We resolve the parameterized complexity of P|r_j,p_j=p|∑U_j with respect to the number of machines, showing W[2]-hardness.
status_evidence.claim: Published STACS 2025 proceedings confirm the W[2]-hardness result, settling the FPT question negatively.
